about: A county page as it was before the fold (prf/new-york/bronx-county.html, origin/main 9c39a7991be3): its example, figures, tables and paragraphs, and the county view the builder wrote from the same USDA files.

old.example: What it costs here at 2027 rates (USDA files read Nov 4, 2026): you pay $269 a year, $2.69 an acre, for 100 acres of grazing at 90% coverage, productivity factor 100, half in April to May and half in June to July, on grid 25125. USDA pays $279 of the $548 full premium. Run over 1951 to 2025 at 2027 rates, it would have paid in 50 of 75 years, an average of $452 a year, or $4.52 an acre. That average is under the full premium of $548; it comes out above your share only because USDA pays the rest. That is the past record, not a forecast, and it leaves out the administrative fee. Example, not a recommendation.

paras: USDA’s 2027 county base values, the same on every grid in the county. Protection per acre is the value times your coverage level times a productivity factor of 60 to 150: grazing at 90% and 100 is $51.75 an acre. USDA sets irrigated hay lower here.

At 90% coverage. The premium is the full rate per $100 of protection; USDA pays 59% at 70%, 59% at 75%, 55% at 80%, 55% at 85%, 51% at 90%. Normal is the grid’s average precipitation for those months. A year counts, of the 75 from 1951 to 2025, when the grid’s index for those months came in under 90% of normal, which is when a 90% policy pays.

The wettest pair of months here is July to August (8.64 in on the grid) and the driest is January to February (6.37 in). Coverage costs least in April to May and most in August to September. The months to insure are the ones when a dry spell costs you grass or hay, not the cheapest ones.

The index for each pair of months as a percent of normal (100 is a normal year), on the grid. Shaded cells came in under 90%, where a 90% policy on those months would have paid. 2026 shows the 6 pairs of months USDA has published so far.

Each grid’s normal precipitation over a year, its driest year since 1951 as a percent of normal, 2025 as a percent of normal, and how many of 75 years as a whole came in under 90%. The driest year on the record here was 1965.

At 90% coverage a pair of months pays when the index comes in under 90% of normal. Over 1951 to 2025, on the grid, that happened in 26 to 37 of 75 years, depending on the months. Run at 2027 rates, $1 of full premium at 90% would have paid back a middle $0.86 across the county’s grids and months. That is the past record, not a forecast.
